title: Grateful Dead Live at Reno Centennial Coliseum on 1982-03-13
lineage: MAC (modified Nakamichi CM-700 mics > Sony TC-D5M on Maxell metal tape) > Nak Dragon playback > Cardas audiophile cables > HHB CDR 800 master CD > Samsung SW-232B extraction (EAC v0.9 beta 4) > tracking (CD Wave) > sector boundary

ai_review.summary: Fast‑tempo Jerry solos and a scorching Stranger→Franklin’s captured on a sparkly but thin audience tape.
ai_review.review: The show is remembered for its wild, high‑energy first half, especially the blistering Stranger > Franklin's sequence and the one‑off Dear Prudence jam. The audience recording is decent with lots of sparkle in the highs, though it sounds a bit thin on the low end and isn’t pristine. Energy tapers after the mid‑set, leaving an overall mixed but memorable performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the show’s high energy and standout jams while noting a drop in later parts; recording is described as decent but not pristine, yielding an overall rating around the mid‑range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape with sparkly highs and thin lows; not the best quality but listenable. Some mention it’s a good sounding Aud, others note the overall tape is sub‑par.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Wild, up‑tempo opening and mid‑first set with fast Jerry solos; energy drops after the Franklin's segment, making the latter part feel less compelling.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight an unusually fast, high‑energy solo style – “Jerry on speed”, “quickest Jerry I have ever heard”, and “Jerry goes absolutely bananas”.
